Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0064-reverse-10", "row_sha256": "064430cb47333cd0986c87bb445f8cf0e45685441e6a0d78b19f88257fc775d5", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you help me put together the family dinner calendar for november 3 through november 16? it’s for the two weeks when i’m covering the evening shift, and i need something i can share with Leonie, not Ellis. please address the finished calendar to Leonie, not Ellis. dinner only, one dinner for each date in order; we don’t need breakfasts, lunches, desserts, or full recipes. there are four of us at home: me, Mara, Dev, and the kids, Kit, who is nine, and June, who is six. actually, that’s four people including me and Dev, yes, Kit and June make four. on november 8 and november 15 my aunt Sal and my cousin Omar will eat with us, so plan those two dinners for six.

we’re trying to keep the whole grocery shop for these dinners to $175 or less, not counting things already in the pantry. i’m going to Cedar Market on november 2, so please give me one compact shopping list grouped by section, with quantities that account for four people on ordinary nights and six on the two guest nights. At home we already have rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, chickpeas, frozen peas, and a bag of carrots; use those where they make sense rather than treating them as items to buy. We also have cooking oil, salt, pepper, and the usual dried spices, but don’t assume we have other ingredients. I’m not asking for an exact receipt or brand recommendations, just a realistic plan that stays under that total.

please keep the meals suitable for the whole family. no peanuts or shellfish at all, and don’t include mushrooms because Kit won’t eat them. June doesn’t like raw onion, so leave raw onion out rather than listing it as an optional topping. We do eat chicken, other meat, and fish, but I’d like three meatless dinners across the two weeks, with at least one of those fully vegan. Fish can appear at most once. Omar avoids dairy, though it isn’t an allergy, so on november 8 and 15 make the main meal dairy-free or give a clearly named dairy-free option that works for him without making a second whole dinner. the other meals don’t have to be dairy-free.

there are a couple of awkward evenings. on november 6 and november 13 Dev won’t be home until after 7:30, so dinner should be ready to reheat, not something that depends on everyone sitting down at the same time or finishing a last-minute cooking step. on november 5 and november 12 i need the dinner to take no more than 25 minutes from starting to serving; please use the pantry items on hand if that helps. One night in each week should be planned leftovers, not a new cooked meal: november 9 and november 16 are the dates that suit us. Please make those entries say what earlier dinner the leftovers come from, and make sure there is enough of that earlier meal for the later date.

Dev reminded me, “don't make Thursdays soup nights while the kids have rehearsal.” So please don’t schedule soup on Thursdays. We have rehearsal every Thursday during this period, and dinner needs to be something the kids can eat before we leave; we usually have about 35 minutes at home. I haven’t listed the rehearsal dates separately because it is the Thursday rule that matters. For the other evenings, a mix of familiar meals and a couple of new ideas is fine, but keep the food approachable and don’t make the same main dish twice. A side dish can repeat if it helps use the carrots or peas.

could the calendar be easy to scan on a phone? Put the date first, then the meal name, a short note about what it includes, and an estimated hands-on or total preparation time. Mark the two guest dinners, the reheating dinners, the quick dinners, and the planned-leftover dinners so I can spot them without reading every note. Don’t add weekday names because I haven’t said which year this is for. Keep the meal descriptions brief enough that the calendar itself doesn’t turn into recipes, and distinguish hands-on work from waiting or reheating time when that difference matters.

I’d also like a short numbered section after the calendar with any simple preparation that can be done on november 2, such as washing or chopping vegetables or setting something aside for a later meal. Keep that section practical and tied to dishes actually on the calendar; don’t make me cook the full dinners in advance. If a planned leftover needs an extra portion cooked, say so on the first date and include that amount in the shopping quantities. Please don’t use an ingredient in the calendar and then leave it out of the shopping list unless it’s in the pantry list above.

at the very end, add one brief note that the prices are estimates and may vary at Cedar Market. Don’t write a personal message to the kids or add nutrition claims. I mainly need an organized calendar and list i can pass along as-is, with all fourteen dates covered and no dinner left blank.", "output": "Create a two-week family dinner calendar for November 3–16, addressed to **Leonie, not Ellis**. Include one dinner for each date in chronological order. Do not include breakfasts, lunches, desserts, or full recipes. The household is Mara, Dev, and their children Kit (nine) and June (six), for four people on ordinary nights. Plan the dinners on November 8 and November 15 for six, as Mara’s aunt Sal and cousin Omar will join.

Keep the grocery shop for these dinners at or below $175, excluding pantry items. The shopping trip is to Cedar Market on November 2. Include one compact shopping list grouped by section, with quantities for four people on ordinary nights and six on the two guest nights. Pantry items already available are rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, chickpeas, frozen peas, carrots, cooking oil, salt, pepper, and usual dried spices. Use these where appropriate and do not assume other ingredients are on hand. The budget should be realistic; exact receipt totals and brand recommendations are not needed.

Follow these food requirements:
1. Do not include peanuts or shellfish. Exclude mushrooms because Kit will not eat them, and leave raw onion out because June dislikes it.
2. Include three meatless dinners across the two weeks, at least one of them fully vegan. Fish may appear no more than once. Chicken and other meat are acceptable.
3. Omar avoids dairy, though it is not an allergy. Make the main meals on November 8 and November 15 dairy-free, or provide a clearly named dairy-free option that works for him without requiring a second full dinner. Other meals need not be dairy-free.
4. Do not repeat the same main dish. Sides may repeat when useful for using carrots or peas.

Account for the schedule. On November 6 and November 13, Dev will return after 7:30, so dinner must be ready to reheat and must not depend on everyone eating at the same time or on a last-minute cooking step. On November 5 and November 12, dinner must take no more than 25 minutes from starting to serving. Use available pantry items where helpful. Plan leftovers rather than a newly cooked dinner on November 9 and November 16. Label each as a planned-leftover dinner, identify the earlier dinner it comes from, and ensure that the earlier meal includes enough food for the later date.

Do not schedule soup on Thursdays. Dev’s request was, “don't make Thursdays soup nights while the kids have rehearsal.” Rehearsal takes place every Thursday in this period, and dinner should be something the children can eat before leaving; the family usually has about 35 minutes at home. Do not add weekday names, since no year has been specified. Other evenings may include familiar meals and a couple of new ideas; keep the food approachable.

Make the calendar easy to scan on a phone. For each date, list the meal name, a brief description of what it includes, and estimated hands-on or total preparation time. Clearly mark guest dinners, reheating dinners, quick dinners, and planned-leftover dinners. Keep descriptions brief rather than writing recipes, and distinguish hands-on time from waiting or reheating time when relevant.

After the calendar, add a short numbered section of practical preparation that can be done on November 2, such as washing or chopping vegetables or setting something aside for a later meal. Tie each task to a dish on the calendar; do not suggest cooking full dinners in advance. If a planned leftover requires an extra portion cooked, state the amount on the earlier dinner’s date and include it in the shopping quantities. Every ingredient used in the calendar must either appear in the shopping list or be listed among the pantry items above.

End with one brief note that prices are estimates and may vary at Cedar Market. Do not add nutrition claims or a personal message to the children. Cover all fourteen dates without leaving a dinner blank."}]
